learningObjective: Determine whether two adjacent loops with a producer-consumer dependence can be legally fused into a single loop nest.

canonicalClaims.claim: Loop fusion is legal only when no fused iteration requires a value that would be produced by a later iteration of the fused loop; i.e., no forward-crossing flow dependence exists between the producer and consumer.
conditions: The two loops have compatible trip counts (equal, or matched via peel/shift).
The iteration order is preserved after fusion.
No cross-loop dependence points backward in the fused iteration order.
nonImplications: Does not imply matching trip counts alone is sufficient for legality.
Does not imply fusion is impossible when a cross-iteration dependence exists — peel/shift or pipelining may restore legality.

misconceptions.claim: Matching trip counts are sufficient to legalize loop fusion.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Trip count is a necessary structural condition; legality also requires dependence analysis to preclude forward-crossing dependences.

misconceptions.claim: If two loops iterate in the same order and touch a common array, fusion is always safe.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Same-order iteration does not remove forward-crossing flow dependences (e.g., reading B[i+1] in iteration i).

misconceptions.claim: Loop fusion requires that both loops write to the same array.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion joins iteration spaces, not write targets. Two loops writing to different arrays are commonly fused (producer-consumer fusion).

misconceptions.claim: A read of B[i-1] in the consumer is a fusion blocker.
misconceptions.whyWrong: B[i-1] is a *backward-crossing* read; in the fused loop, B[i-1] is produced in the previous iteration and is available. This does not block fusion.

implementationFacts: MLIR affine dialect uses affine access maps to check fusion legality automatically.
Loop peel + shift is a standard rewrite that can convert some illegal fusions into legal ones.
performanceScenarios: Fusing a normalization producer with a subsequent activation consumer is legal when the consumer reads only B[i] (same-iteration flow) — this is the pattern used in LayerNorm+activation fusion.
